She is still raw from the breakup.
Acknowledge that she is hurting, then offer a limit you can manage, such as one real check-in this week.
My friend asked why I unfollowed her online.
Tell her you were reducing what you see online and it was not meant as a public statement about the friendship.
I actually unfollowed because her posts about me annoyed me.
Be honest that the posts bothered you, and name the kind of posting you do not want about yourself.
My mother sent me a long apology letter.
Thank her for writing it and take time before responding if you need it.
I am not ready to forgive her yet.
Tell her you received it and need more time; you do not have to offer forgiveness on her timeline.
My roommate wants to adopt a dog, but I do not.
Tell them a dog affects both people in the home, so you cannot agree unless the care plan works for you too.
They say they will do all the work.
Explain that noise, guests, travel, and shared space still affect you even if they handle feeding and walks.
I want to invite my neighbor for dinner, but we barely know each other.
Keep it low-pressure: "I am making pasta Thursday and would be glad to have you over if you are free."
My partner forgot our anniversary.
Tell them you are hurt because the date mattered to you, rather than testing whether they will guess why.
I miss my best friend, but she has a new baby.
Send a short message that does not require a big reply: tell her you miss her and are thinking of her family.
My sister called me selfish for skipping her brunch.
Tell her you understand she was disappointed, but one missed brunch does not justify calling you selfish.
I need to ask my partner to pick up groceries.
Ask for the items and a timeframe directly, rather than hoping they notice the empty fridge.
They are already at the store, and we only need eggs and coffee.
Text: "Could you grab eggs and coffee while you are there? Thanks."
I want to invite a friend to lunch after we argued.
Send a short invitation that leaves room for them to decline: "Would you be open to lunch this week?"
I need to acknowledge the argument first.
Write, "I have been thinking about our argument, and I am sorry for my part. Would you be open to lunch this week?"
I made fun of my husband's cooking, and he looked hurt.
Apologize for the joke and say you saw it land badly; then thank him for making dinner.
My dad makes jokes about my job in front of people.
Tell him privately that the jokes land as disrespectful and ask him to stop making them around others.
My roommate used my mug again after I asked her not to.
Tell her plainly that the mug is off-limits and ask her to choose another one.
My colleague confided in me, and I do not know how to respond.
Thank them for trusting you and ask whether they want advice or simply someone to hear them out.
Can you write a gentle reminder about splitting the bill?
Write: "Hey, your half for dinner was $24. Could you send it when you get a chance?"
How can I make small talk at my partner's work party?
Ask people how they know your partner or what they have been working on, then follow the answer.
My dad wants to give advice about my apartment search.
Thank him and tell him what kind of help you want, such as reviewing a lease rather than choosing neighborhoods.
He already sent me twelve listings.
Thank him for the effort, pick out any useful ones, and ask him to pause new listings until you review these.
My friend says I interrupt too much.
Thank them for saying it, then practice pausing after they finish before you respond.
My friend asked whether her baby is cute.
Tell her the baby is adorable if you mean it, and mention one real detail you noticed.
The baby is mostly crying in the photo.
Say, "That tiny furious face is memorable. You have got a strong-willed one."
My cousin wants to borrow money again.
You can say no without defending it: "I cannot lend money right now, but I hope things ease up."
My cousin wants to bring her boyfriend to my birthday dinner.
Tell her whether you have room for an extra guest before she assumes he is included.
It is a reservation for eight, and all eight seats are taken.
Tell her the reservation is full and you would be glad to meet him another time.
I need to say no to a friend staying on my couch.
Say that you cannot host overnight right now, without inventing a complicated excuse.
They asked just for one night after a concert.
Keep the boundary if it still does not work, and suggest they arrange a ride or another place to stay.
My friend forgot to invite me to her birthday dinner.
Ask her about it privately if the friendship matters to you, because guessing will make the hurt louder.
She says the restaurant only had six seats.
Tell her you understand the limit while also saying you felt sad to be left out.
A friend wants to talk every night, and I do not.
Set a rhythm you can keep: nightly calls are too much, but once or twice a week would work.
I forgot to respond to a wedding invitation.
Reply today, apologize for the delay, and give a clear yes or no without a long story.
My mom wants a phone call every morning.
Offer a schedule you can sustain, such as Sunday calls and a few texts during the week.
I want to ask a friend why she is avoiding me.
Ask gently whether something has changed between you, and leave room for an honest answer.
She has been replying, just not making plans.
Mention that pattern specifically and ask whether she wants more space or simply has less availability right now.
I promised my nephew I would play soccer with him.
Keep the promise if you can, because he will remember that you made time for him.
It is pouring rain, and he is six.
Offer an indoor game now and set a new soccer time for the next dry day.
I am irritated that my partner left without saying goodbye.
Tell them you felt dismissed when they left without a word and ask for a quick goodbye next time.
They were rushing to catch a train.
Acknowledge the rush, then ask for a two-second text or wave when that happens.
I need to tell my friend I cannot host her cat.
Say you cannot host the cat this time, even if you have a soft spot for its suspicious little face.
I want to invite my parents over, but my place is messy.
Invite them anyway and set expectations: "Come Sunday for soup; the apartment is lived-in, not staged."
My friend asked me to feed her fish while she travels.
Ask for the dates, feeding instructions, and a backup contact before you agree.
She will be gone for two weeks, and I can only do the first five days.
Offer the five days clearly and tell her she will need another person for the rest of the trip.
My friend sent a meme while I was venting.
Tell them you needed them to stay with what you were saying, because the meme made you feel brushed aside.
I need to reschedule dinner with my parents.
Tell them promptly that you need to move dinner and offer two alternative dates.
My dad gets annoyed by vague plans.
Give exact choices, such as Tuesday at seven or Saturday at six.
My friend only calls when they need help moving.
Say yes only if you want to, and mention that you would also like to see them when no boxes are involved.
I forgot my sister's recital tonight. What should I say?
Apologize without excuses: say you missed it, know it mattered, and ask how it went.
I laughed when my friend tripped, and now she is mad.
Acknowledge that it hurt: "I laughed before I checked whether you were okay. I am sorry."
My friend said my haircut looks brave.
You can tease back: "Thanks, I will add it to my list of courageous acts."
My friend complains that I reply slowly.
Explain your usual reply window and reassure them that delay is not a measure of how much you value them.
My aunt gave me a gift I do not like.
Thank her for thinking of you; you do not need to pretend the gift is perfect.
My friend invited me camping this weekend.
Accept if you want to go, or decline soon so they can plan food and rides.
I want to go, but only for Saturday because I hate sleeping in tents.
Tell them you are in for Saturday and will head home before the overnight part.
My mother reads my messages over my shoulder.
Move your screen and tell her you want your messages to stay private, even when you are sitting together.
My dad apologized, but he keeps doing the same thing.
Tell him the apology would mean more with a change in behavior, and name the behavior you need changed.
My brother criticizes every restaurant I choose.
Hand him the choice next time, then ask that he skip the running review of everyone else's pick.
My partner says I am distracted at dinner.
Ask what moments make them feel ignored, then agree on a phone-free part of dinner if that is the issue.
They mean I keep checking work messages.
Tell them you will silence work alerts during dinner unless you are expecting something urgent.
My partner wants to spend every holiday with their family.
Tell them you want a plan that includes both families and some time just for the two of you.
Their family lives five hours away, so splitting one day is impossible.
Plan whole holidays in rotation, and decide the schedule well before travel arrangements are made.
My mother criticized my clothes at lunch.
Tell her you are comfortable with what you wore and do not want comments about your clothes.
She said she was only being helpful.
Say that help is useful when requested, and you are asking her to leave your clothes out of the conversation.
I called my mom by the wrong name in a text.
Correct it with a quick apology, then blame neither fate nor your phone for your name management.
My roommate asks why I lock my bedroom door.
Tell them you lock it for privacy and peace of mind, not because you are accusing them of anything.
They say it makes the apartment feel unfriendly.
Say you understand the feeling, but a locked bedroom is a normal boundary and you are keeping it.
I told my friend I could babysit Saturday.
Confirm the hours and any instructions so there are no surprises.
I just learned I have a work deadline that day.
Tell your friend as soon as possible that you need to retract the offer and apologize for the inconvenience.
I accidentally shared a secret my friend told me.
Tell your friend exactly what you shared, apologize, and do not ask them to make you feel better about it.
I want to praise my partner without sounding cheesy.
Name something concrete: "I noticed how patient you were with your niece today. She clearly trusts you."
I want to tell Leo I like him.
Tell Leo directly that you enjoy spending time with him and would like to take him on a date.
We work together, so I do not want it to be awkward.
Ask once outside work, make it easy to decline, and say you will keep things normal either way.
I want to invite my sister to a concert.
Ask whether she wants to go before buying a ticket, especially if she is busy lately.
It is tomorrow, and the ticket is extra.
Send: "I have an extra ticket for tomorrow night. Want to join me? No pressure if it is too short notice."
My family expects me to host Thanksgiving.
Tell them early whether you can host, because hosting is work and should be a choice.
I can host, but I will not cook for sixteen people alone.
Agree to host and assign dishes to guests before anyone assumes you are providing the full meal.
I feel guilty saying no to a family trip.
Guilt can show up even when your choice is reasonable. Decline the trip clearly and avoid negotiating against yourself.
My uncle keeps commenting on my apartment size.
Reply that the apartment suits you, then steer the conversation to something other than your square footage.
My partner bought concert tickets without asking me.
Thank them for the thought, then explain that you need to check your schedule before plans are purchased for both of you.
The concert is for a band I actually hate.
Tell them you appreciate the gesture but do not want to go, and offer to help them find someone else who would enjoy the ticket.
I am annoyed that my friend brought an extra guest.
Tell them afterward that you needed a heads-up before adding people to plans you arranged.
My dad borrowed my drill and has not returned it.
Ask when he can bring it back, using the drill's name rather than a vague reminder.
He says he might need it next weekend too.
Tell him you need it back before then, and ask him to buy or borrow another one for his project.
My friend made a group plan on a night I already said I was busy.
Tell them you cannot make it and avoid treating the plan as a personal slight without more information.
They used my apartment for it without asking.
Tell them they cannot use your apartment as a venue without your permission, regardless of whether you are there.
I need to cancel a coffee date because I am exhausted.
Cancel honestly and suggest another day: "I am too worn out to be good company tonight. Could we reschedule?"
I do not know what to say when a friend tells me their dog died.
Say that you are sorry they lost their dog and that you know how much the dog meant to them.
My boyfriend gets quiet whenever we disagree.
Ask whether he needs a short break or feels unable to talk, then set a time to return to the issue.
I told my roommate her music was too loud.
Ask her to lower it or use headphones, and keep the request about the volume rather than her taste.
She said I am loud too when I cook.
Acknowledge that cooking can be noisy, then suggest quiet hours that apply to both of you.
My partner criticized me in front of friends.
Tell them afterward that the public criticism embarrassed you and ask them to raise concerns privately.
They say they were joking.
Say the intent may have been playful, but the impact was embarrassing and you need them to stop.
My grandma repeats the same stories.
Let her tell the story when you can, and ask one new question about it to keep the moment warm.
My roommate leaves passive-aggressive notes.
Ask to discuss the issue face-to-face because notes make it harder to understand what they need.
The latest note says I am allergic to washing pans.
Reply that you will wash the pan, and ask them to bring complaints to you directly instead of turning them into jokes.
My sister borrowed my car without asking.
Tell her she needs permission before using your car, even when she assumes you are not using it.
She says it was an emergency because she was late for yoga.
Say that being late for yoga does not make it an emergency, and restate that the car is not hers to take.
My friend said my new glasses look different.
Ask whether they mean different in a good way if their tone was unclear.
They said, "Different is one word for it."
Reply, "Excellent, I was aiming for memorable rather than invisible."
My cousin keeps bringing up my ex.
Ask your cousin to stop mentioning your ex because you do not want that person to be a standing topic.
She says she is only trying to cheer me up.
Tell her you appreciate the intention, but discussing your ex has the opposite effect.
My friend says I never initiate plans.
Acknowledge that they have been carrying the planning, then invite them to something specific this week.
I am free only Wednesday morning.
Ask whether they want coffee Wednesday morning at a place near them.
I am hosting game night, and one friend always arrives late.
Tell everyone the game will start at a set time, then begin then rather than waiting for one person.
She says starting without her is rude.
Tell her you want her there, but the group should not lose an hour whenever she arrives late.
I sent my friend a joke about his new beard.
Ask whether the joke bothered him if he seems off, rather than assuming he found it funny.
He replied, "Wow, brutal."
Reply, "Fair, I went too hard. Your beard deserves a better review than that."
My partner leaves dishes for me because I work from home.
Point out that being home is not the same as being available, and agree on a dish routine together.
My brother brought up politics at dinner again.
Say you are not discussing politics over dinner, then change the subject before the table becomes a debate stage.
I want to send flowers to a friend who lost her job.
Send them with a note that says you are thinking of her and believe she will find her footing.
She hates flowers because of pollen.
Send a favorite snack, coffee, or a handwritten note instead.
My friend copied my vacation plan.
You can let it be a compliment, unless they are asking you to plan every detail for them too.
I am nervous about meeting my friend's new partner.
Be curious rather than performative: greet them warmly and ask what they have been enjoying together.
I snapped at my partner because I was hungry.
Own the snap directly: "I spoke sharply, and that was unfair. I am sorry."
I do not want to lend my favorite jacket.
Say, "I am keeping that one for myself, but I can help you find another option."
Someone I am dating wants to meet my friends already.
Tell them you are enjoying getting to know them and would rather wait before blending social circles.
My cousin is visiting Saturday, but I need to work until noon.
Tell her you would love to see her after noon and ask whether that timing works.
Actually, she is arriving at ten and cannot change it.
Let her know you will be working until noon, so she can make herself comfortable quietly or meet you later.
My sister asked me to keep a secret from our parents.
Ask what the secret involves before agreeing to keep it, especially if it could affect anyone's safety or finances.
It is only that she is planning a surprise party for them.
Keep that secret and enjoy having a rare reason to be mysterious at family dinner.
My friend got the promotion I wanted.
Congratulate them plainly; disappointment and happiness for them can exist at the same time.
I need an excuse to leave a party early.
Use the truth in a small form: "I am heading out, but I am glad I came by."
I need a funny reply to my friend's terrible parking photo.
Try: "Bold of you to park by vibes instead of lines."
My partner wants to talk right when I get home.
Tell them you need twenty minutes to decompress, then commit to talking after that.
They say waiting makes them feel ignored.
Reassure them you are not avoiding them, and make the return time concrete so it does not feel indefinite.
My friend wants to borrow my expensive camera.
Say no if you are not comfortable lending it, because the price and sentimental value make that reasonable.
She only needs it for an afternoon wedding.
Keep the no, or offer to attend and take a few photos yourself if that genuinely works for you.
My partner wants to share locations all the time.
Say that constant location sharing does not work for you, and discuss what reassurance they are actually seeking.
My partner and I argued about being late.
Talk about what each of you needs around timing, then agree on when to send an update.
I want to reconnect with an old friend after two years.
Send a simple note: "I thought of you today and wondered how you have been. I would love to catch up."
I am meeting my friend's parents for the first time.
Bring a small host gift if appropriate, arrive on time, and let your friend guide you on formality.
They told me not to bring anything.
Follow that request and bring only yourself, on time and ready to be present.
My friend keeps sending voice notes during work.
Let them know you listen after work, but text is better for anything time-sensitive during the day.
My mother offered to pay for our vacation.
Thank her and ask whether the offer comes with any expectations before accepting.
She expects to choose the entire itinerary.
Decide whether that trade works for you; if not, thank her and pay for your own trip.
Can you help me decline a third date kindly?
Say, "I enjoyed meeting you, but I do not feel the connection I am looking for. I wish you well."
I want to bring soup to a sick friend.
Ask whether soup would be useful and check for dietary restrictions before making it.
She is lactose intolerant, and I already made cream soup.
Keep the cream soup for yourself and offer to bring a dairy-free meal instead.
My niece thinks my jokes are terrible.
Tell her your comedy has a selective audience, then accept that she is currently not on the list.
My friend is quiet after I teased them.
Check in directly: "I may have pushed that joke too far. Did it hurt?"
My brother asked to stay at my place for a month.
Ask what dates he means and whether a month works for your household before agreeing.
I can only manage one week, and he is between apartments.
Offer the week clearly, and tell him you cannot extend it beyond that date.
I told my aunt I would call her Sunday.
Call Sunday if possible, or message before then if you need to change the plan.
Sunday is tomorrow, but I have a migraine.
Message her now that you are unwell and ask whether another day this week would work.
My friend keeps correcting my stories.
Tell them the constant corrections make you feel policed, even when the details are small.
He says accuracy matters.
Agree that accuracy matters, then ask him to save minor corrections unless they change the point of the story.
My mother-in-law rearranges my kitchen when she visits.
Ask her to leave the kitchen as she finds it, because you need your home to work the way you set it up.
My girlfriend says I never ask about her day.
Ask her about today specifically, then listen without turning it into a comparison with your own day.
I want to check on my aunt after her surgery.
Send a brief message asking how she is feeling and whether she needs anything dropped off.
She does not like visitors when she feels rough.
Offer a doorstep drop-off and make clear that she does not need to answer the door.
I do not want hugs from one coworker.
Step back and say, "I am not a hug person, but it is good to see you."
My partner wants me to meet their friends tonight.
Tell them whether you have the energy for it and suggest another night if you do not.
I am tired, but I have already canceled twice.
Go for a short, defined time if you can, and tell your partner in advance that you will leave early.
My friend has not answered in a week. Should I double text?
Send one light follow-up if you need clarity, then give them room to respond.
My uncle keeps asking when I will have kids.
Reply, "That is personal, and I would rather talk about something else."
My dad texted, "Call me."
Call him when you can, or send a quick message asking whether everything is okay.
He tends to turn every call into an hour-long lecture.
Reply that you have ten minutes now and call within that limit.
My brother apologized for breaking my headphones.
Thank him for apologizing and ask how he plans to replace them.
He offered his old headphones instead.
Tell him you need a replacement of similar quality, not a pair he no longer wants.
My uncle keeps forwarding alarming news stories.
Ask him not to send those stories to you because they make your phone feel like an alarm bell.
I do not want to sound rude.
Phrase it warmly: "I know you mean well, but I am taking a break from heavy news links."
I want to ask a friend for a ride to the airport.
Ask early, include the time and airport, and make it easy for them to say no.
My flight leaves at six in the morning.
Acknowledge the early hour and say you completely understand if they cannot do it.
My sister texted me a recipe that looks awful.
Thank her for sending it and avoid reviewing the meal like a television judge.
She asked whether I will make it.
Say you are not sure it is your kind of dish, but you would love to hear how hers turns out.
My best friend forgot I hate surprise parties.
Tell them you appreciate the effort but surprises make you anxious, so you would rather celebrate another way.
Everyone is already hiding in my living room.
Step in, thank everyone briefly, and ask for a low-key evening instead of pretending you are enjoying the surprise.
I want to apologize to Maya for missing her call.
Text Maya that you saw the missed call, apologize, and ask whether she still wants to talk.
She called because her cat was at the vet, so that sounds too casual.
Say, "I am sorry I missed you when you were dealing with that. How is your cat now?"
My friend wants me to join a running club.
Tell them whether you are interested, and do not agree just to avoid disappointing them.
I want to see them, but I do not run.
Suggest meeting them for coffee after their run instead.
Can I leave a group chat without making it dramatic?
Yes. Write, "I am trimming notifications, so I am stepping out. See you individually."
My partner asked whether I am upset.
Answer honestly with the smallest true version of what you feel, rather than saying nothing is wrong when something is.
I am upset, but I need an hour before talking.
Tell them you are upset and need an hour, then name a time when you will come back to the conversation.
My friend canceled our plans for the fourth time.
Ask whether they still want to make plans, because repeated cancellations make it hard to keep holding the time.
I need to ask my roommate to replace the milk.
Ask directly: "Could you pick up milk this week since you finished the last of it?"
I want to invite my grandfather to lunch.
Offer a clear day and time, and choose a place that is easy for him to get to.
He does not drive anymore.
Offer to pick him up or meet near his home.
I need to cancel on my book club.
Tell the group you cannot make it and mention whether you will still read the book for next time.
I have not read a page.
Skip the claim about reading it and simply say you cannot make this meeting.
I want to tell my neighbor their tree branches are over my fence.
Mention it calmly and ask whether they can trim the branches when they have time.
The branches are dropping fruit onto my car.
Add that the falling fruit is damaging your car, so you need a date for the trimming rather than an open-ended promise.
My friend is moving away and I feel weirdly angry.
The anger may be carrying sadness about the change. Tell them you are happy for them and will miss them nearby.
How do I say I cannot be someone's emergency contact?
Say, "I care about you, but I cannot take on that responsibility. Please choose someone who can."
I feel bad that I cannot attend my friend's art show.
Tell them you are sorry to miss it and ask whether there is a way to see the work another day.
The show is only open one night.
Ask them to send photos afterward and celebrate the show with them over coffee later.
Use British spelling. Write: The color of the center changed.
The colour of the centre changed.
Write a note saying the museum opens at nine.
The museum opens at 9 a.m.
Correction: it closes at nine and opens at ten.
The museum opens at 10 a.m. and closes at 9 p.m.
Explain HTTP more simply and without abbreviations.
It is a set of rules that browsers and websites use to exchange information.
Make this invitation formal: Come by Friday.
You are cordially invited to visit on Friday.
Friday is wrong; the event is on Sunday, and the tone should be casual.
Come by on Sunday!
I asked for a shape that is both a perfect circle and a square. Is that possible?
No single Euclidean shape can be both a perfect circle and a square.
What is the difference between affect and effect?
Affect is usually a verb meaning to influence, while effect is usually a noun meaning a result.
I only need the correct word in The rain had no blank on attendance.
Use effect.
Plan a workout using dumbbells.
Combine goblet squats, rows, presses, Romanian deadlifts, and carries in a full-body session.
My wrist is injured, and I was told to avoid weights. Suggest a gentle walk instead.
Take a short, level walk at an easy pace and stop if the injury becomes uncomfortable.
What does the bat do at night?
Do you mean the flying mammal or a piece of sports equipment?
The flying mammal.
A bat may leave its roost at night to find food and water.
Give me a slogan for a fast delivery service.
From our door to yours, right on time.
Forget speed. The service is for careful art transport.
Handled with care, delivered with confidence.
We cannot meet on Tuesdays, so the Tuesday appointment is a mistake. Suggest the next weekday.
Move the appointment to Wednesday.
I need gluten-free bread. Is ordinary sourdough acceptable?
Ordinary sourdough is not gluten-free, so choose bread specifically certified as gluten-free.
What should I bring for a rainy hike?
Bring a waterproof jacket, sturdy footwear, warm layers, water, food, and a map.
The hike was cancelled. What should I bring to an indoor swim?
Pack a swimsuit, towel, goggles, toiletries, and a change of clothes.
The alarm must be silent but still alert me. What setting should I use?
Use vibration with sound disabled.
I meant two and a half hours, not 2.5 minutes. How many minutes is that?
Two and a half hours is 150 minutes.
Send a reminder that payment is overdue.
Your payment is overdue; please arrange payment as soon as possible.
It is not overdue yet. Remind them it is due tomorrow.
This is a reminder that your payment is due tomorrow.
They refers to Alex alone, whose pronouns are they and them. Rewrite Alex said Alex would come.
Alex said they would come.
The audience is now children aged eight, not engineers. Explain a database.
A database is an organized collection of information that a computer can quickly find and update.
Current refers to water movement, not electricity. Define it.
A current is the directed movement of water through a larger body of water.
I wrote plus by mistake. What is 17 minus 9?
17 minus 9 equals 8.
Match means the thing used to start a fire. Give its plural.
The plural is matches.
What does Python eat?
Do you mean a python snake or the Python programming language?
The snake, and keep it suitable for a child.
A python eats animals such as rodents and birds by swallowing them whole.
By the second one, I mean the blue folder after the red folder. Which folder should I archive?
Archive the blue folder.
Summarize the causes and effects of the delay.
Please share the material that describes the delay.
I only need this sentence shortened: Rain delayed the game for two hours.
Rain delayed the game by two hours.
Draft a long response accepting the offer.
I am pleased to accept the offer and appreciate the opportunity to join the team. I look forward to discussing the next steps.
Make it one sentence and decline instead.
Thank you for the offer, but I must decline.
They refers to the committee members. Should the verb be is or are?
Use are because committee members is plural in this sentence.
Put this in plain language: The agreement shall terminate upon insolvency.
The agreement ends if a party becomes unable to pay its debts.
That wording is too casual. Rewrite Please send it today in a formal tone.
Please ensure that it is sent today.
My hotel budget changed to 90 euros a night. What should I filter for?
Set the nightly price ceiling to 90 euros and filter by your required location and amenities.
Should I file this under invoices or receipts?
What kind of document is it?
It is a bill from a supplier that we have not paid.
File it under invoices.
The upbeat version feels wrong. Rewrite We will miss him in a somber tone.
His absence will be deeply felt.
Explain inflation in one plain sentence.
Inflation is a general rise in prices that reduces what your money can buy.
Write a playful birthday message for Luis.
Happy birthday, Luis! May your cake be large and your chores be small.
Luis prefers a straightforward message with no joke.
Happy birthday, Luis. I hope you have a wonderful day.
What happened after Jordan called Casey?
I need more context to know what happened after the call.
Casey, not Jordan, made the call; afterward Jordan sent the file.
After Casey called Jordan, Jordan sent the file.
Skip the metaphor. State literally what a firewall does.
A firewall monitors network traffic and blocks connections that violate its rules.
Explain photosynthesis again, but for a six-year-old.
Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make their own food and release oxygen.
In the truck passed the trailer before it stopped, I mean the trailer stopped. Rewrite it.
The truck passed the trailer before the trailer stopped.
Recommend a red wine for the stew.
A dry red such as Merlot or Côtes du Rhône would suit a hearty stew.
No alcohol can be used. What liquid should replace the wine?
Replace the wine with beef or vegetable stock plus a small splash of vinegar.
Which port should I use?
Do you mean a network port, a harbour, or the left side of a vessel?
The left side of a boat; what colour marks it?
A boat's port side is marked with red navigation lights.
Stop debugging the program. Just explain what permission denied means.
Permission denied means the current user or process is not allowed to access the requested resource.
